sentences.text: Santanaraptor was a small carnivore about 1.25 meters long, known from a juvenile partial skeleton containing tail vertebrae, pelvic and leg bones, and soft tissue.
Skin impressions under the left foot show preserved scales, while other fossilized soft tissues include epidermis, muscle fibers, and possibly blood vessels.
It is presumed to have had long arms, three-fingered hands, and slim hindlimbs, similar to Dilong and Guanlong.
Skin impressions under the left foot show preserved scales.
Fossilized soft tissues include epidermis, muscle fibers, and possibly blood vessels.
The species Santanaraptor placidus was first described by Kellner in 1999.
The holotype fossil was unearthed in 1996 from the Romualdo Formation in Ceará State, northeastern Brazil.
The species was originally considered a maniraptor when first described.
Santanaraptor is thought to be closely related to the Early Jurassic coelurosaur Ornitholestes based on similarities in the ischium.

Santanaraptor is now classified as a basal coelurosaur based on features found on the femur, rather than a maniraptoran theropod. Today, Santanaraptor is considered a basal Coelurosauria due to specific features found on the femur.

Santanaraptor lived in South America during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago. Santanaraptor placidus lived in South America during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 108 million years ago.
Fossils were found in the Santana Formation across Pernambuco, Piauí, and Ceará states in northeastern Brazil.
The time range for Santanaraptor is estimated between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
The classification of Santanaraptor as a tyrannosauroid is debated because its supposed tyrannosauroid traits are widespread in Coelurosauria and its foot resembles noasaurids.
A 2025 study suggests Santanaraptor could be either a megaraptoran within Tyrannosauroidea or an early branching maniraptoromorph outside that group, depending on the phylogenetic method used.
